key_insight: Pre-alloyed powder blends plus remelting and heat treatment can produce chemically homogeneous, single-β Ti-Nb-Fe-Sn alloys by PBF-LB despite using a coarse 70 μm layer thickness.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable route to low-modulus titanium parts with tunable strength and stiffness for biomedical and structural applications.
method: Blend Ti-42Nb, Ti-20Nb-15Fe, and Ti-20Nb-20Sn master-alloy powders with commercial-purity Ti
Fabricate Ti-Nb-Fe-Sn parts by PBF-LB using 70 μm layers and layer remelting
Apply 1000 °C/2 h heat treatment followed by water quenching to homogenize composition and stabilize β microstructure
evidence_signal: After heat treatment, all compositions showed low porosity, homogeneous elemental distribution, single-β microstructures, hardness of 224–268 HV, yield strength of 468–691 MPa, and Young's modulus of 63–81 GPa.
watch_item: Non-monotonic grain-size evolution was not fully explained, so composition changes may trigger complex grain-growth behavior that needs further process control.
paper_title: Designing Homogeneous Ti-Nb-Fe-Sn $β$ Titanium Alloys by PBF-LB: A Pre-Alloyed Powder Blend Strategy
